newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada T-bills open mixed, short-term issues gain.
newsitem.headline: Canada T-bills open mixed, short-term issues gain.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened mixed in very quiet trade on Tuesday, with investors favoring shorter-term issues amid uncertainty about the near-term direction of rates and a firmer dollar, analysts said.

"The activity rate yesterday was extremely low, probably as low as we've seen for a long, long time. I think part of that is still carrying over today as well," said one T-bill trader with a bank-owned brokerage.
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.23 percent from 3.25 percent at Friday's close.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill softened to yield 3.60 percent from 3.58 percent at Monday's close.
The trader said accounts were shying away from the six-month portion of the curve ahead of today's weekly T-bill tender because of recent squeezes which have taken place in that term area.
The Government of Canada this afternoon will auction C$4.8 billion in three-month, six-month and one-year T-bills. Results of today's auction will be released at 1315 EDT/1715 GMT.
The one-year T-bill traded with a yield 4.24 percent, unchanged from the close of trading on Monday.
The call loan rate traded at 3.05 percent, near the center of the Bank of Canada's 2.75-3.25 percent target range.
